references.text: Esau runs toward Jacob, embraces him, falls on his neck, and kisses him, and they weep. This mirrors the emotional reunion and embrace between Joseph and Benjamin.
Joseph goes up to meet his father Israel in Goshen, falls on his neck, and weeps for a long time. The same expression ('falling on the neck and weeping') is used as in Joseph's reunion with Benjamin.
The psalm describes how good and beautiful it is when brothers dwell together in unity, which is reflected in the touching reunion between Joseph and Benjamin.
The prodigal son is embraced by his father who falls on his neck and kisses him, a parallel to the warm and emotional embrace between Joseph and Benjamin.
The Ephesian elders weep, fall on Paul's neck, and kiss him at their farewell. The same physical expression of deep emotional attachment as in Gen 45:14.
The verses together show the transition from inner emotional struggle to outer reunion and complete brotherhood.
